invariants.statement: A non-zero vector v is an eigenvector of A if Av = λv for some scalar λ.
For a real symmetric matrix, A = QΛQᵀ with orthonormal eigenvectors and real eigenvalues.
The power iteration requires a unique dominant eigenvalue in magnitude, so |λ₁| > |λ₂|.
conditions: The initial vector has a non-zero component along v₁

invariants.statement: The iteration uses xₖ₊₁ = A xₖ / ||A xₖ||₂, with the vector normalised each step.
The Rayleigh quotient ρ(x) = xᵀ A x / xᵀ x estimates the eigenvalue associated with x.
The residual r = A x − ρ(x) x measures the quality of an approximate eigenpair, and a small ||r||₂ is a practical stopping test.
conditions: ρ(x) is computed from the same x

invariants.statement: If the initial vector has zero projection onto the dominant eigendirection, the method cannot recover that mode in exact arithmetic.
A negative dominant eigenvalue can cause sign alternation, but the eigendirection still converges up to sign.
